analysis.answer: Current law makes the possession of any amount of cannabis a misdemeanor punishable by up to 90 days in jail. The proposed measure allows adults 21 and older to possess up to one ounce of cannabis without it being an offense, effectively removing criminal penalties for that group and amount.

The measure lowers costs by reducing the resources spent on arresting, prosecuting, and incarcerating individuals for low-level cannabis possession. It may incur a loss of revenue from fines previously collected for misdemeanor possession convictions.

Adults 21 and older benefit by avoiding arrest, legal fees, and jail time for possessing up to one ounce of cannabis. The local criminal justice system benefits from a reduced misdemeanor caseload, freeing up resources.

Without the threat of a misdemeanor charge and jail time, adults 21 and older may be more likely to openly possess and consume cannabis within the one-ounce limit. Law enforcement agencies will reallocate the time and resources previously spent enforcing the possession ban.
The measure addresses the criminalization of low-level cannabis possession. Its mechanism directly reaches this by legalizing the possession of up to one ounce for adults 21 and older.
